evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 備 entry; script forms; 說文; 形義通解; reported inscriptions and manuscripts
evidence.text: The entry displays 備 forms under oracle bone, bronze and manuscript categories without dating its earliest occurrence. It quotes Shuowen’s ‘慎也。从人，𤰈聲’ and ‘𠈍，古文備’. CUHK interprets the graph as 人 plus 𤰈, with 𤰈 also phonetic, and the human figure as carrying an arrow container, linking that image to preparedness. It reports bronze uses glossed as equipped/complete and for use, loans of 備 for 佩 and 箙, and Warring States manuscript readings as 服. These reported contexts do not establish the spoken word’s earliest sense or a complete semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 備

evidence.field: lookup interface scope and data access instructions
evidence.text: The official lookup page says its interface provides individual-character Unihan properties, including readings, and directs users to the Unicode Character Database for the latest downloadable data. This general page was accessible; the requested codepoint-specific lookup pages were not.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup

evidence.field: U+5099 kMandarin; U+7B99 kMandarin rows (rows 36582 and 136848)
evidence.text: Local rows give 備 bèi and 箙 fú. This is current Mandarin metadata, not evidence for an ancient sound relationship. The inspected exact codepoint-specific Unicode records for 備 (U+5099), 箙 (U+7B99), and 𤰈 (U+24C08) could not be opened, so this local evidence is not offered as externally verified click-through evidence. The local extract has no row for 𤰈.
evidence.title: Unicode Unihan record lookup for 備 (attempted; inaccessible)

evidence.field: entries for 備 and 箙
evidence.text: The local version 1.1 table gives 備 bèi, MC bijH, OC *[b]rək-s (‘complete (adj.)’) and 箙 fú, MC bjuwk, OC *[b]ək (‘a quiver’). This compares the lexical characters 備 and 箙; it does not supply a reading for 𤰈 or establish that the pictured object was named or pronounced 箙. The official PDF was attempted but inaccessible in this browser invocation.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (attempted; inaccessible)

search_audit.outcome: Opened Unicode’s general Unihan lookup page, which documents the database lookup and download route. Character-specific pages were inaccessible, and the ZIP endpoint returned an unsupported-content-type error. The Baxter–Sagart PDF remained inaccessible; no secondary snippet was treated as inspected evidence.

gaps: Unicode’s official character-specific records for 備, 箙 and 𤰈 could not be inspected, so local Unihan values are not externally verified here; no current reading for 𤰈 was obtained.
The official Baxter–Sagart PDF could not be opened in this invocation. Local version 1.1 rows compare 備 and 箙 but do not provide a reconstruction for 𤰈.
Shuowen and CUHK assign 𤰈 a phonetic role, but an independent historical reading for 𤰈 was not verified. Modern readings and the 備–箙 comparison cannot establish that relation.

CUHK reports 備 written for 箙 (‘quiver’) in a bronze inscription. This whole-graph loan does not establish the pictured container’s original name or pronunciation, nor prove a sound match between 𤰈 and 箙.

The inspected CUHK entry reports oracle, bronze and manuscript categories, but does not date the earliest graph. It reports varied contexts and glosses without establishing the earliest spoken sense or a fully dated semantic sequence.

The 1956 adoption and the specific 俻-to-备 derivation were not rechecked in this invocation; prior dossier research says the scheme confirms 备（備）, while a direct derivation from 俻 remains unestablished.
